qualitative.filing_summary_10k: Apple's fiscal 2025 10-K reports total net sales of $416.2 billion, up 6% year-over-year, driven by growth in Services (up 14%) and iPhone, Mac, and iPad, partially offset by declines in Wearables, Home and Accessories. Total gross margin percentage rose to 46.9% from 46.2%, though product margins faced pressure from tariffs and product mix. The filing discusses new U.S. tariffs on imports from several countries beginning in fiscal Q2 2025, a lower effective tax rate partly due to a prior-year State Aid Decision impact, and a capital return program including an increased $100 billion share repurchase authorization and a raised quarterly dividend to $0.26 per share.
qualitative.filing_summary_10q: This Q3 fiscal 2026 10-Q (quarter ended June 27, 2026) shows total net sales of $109.4 billion for the quarter, up from $94.0 billion a year earlier, with net income of $29.8 billion versus $23.4 billion in the prior-year quarter. For the nine months ended June 27, 2026, net sales were $364.4 billion and net income was $101.5 billion, both higher than the comparable 2025 period. The balance sheet shows total assets of $383.3 billion and shareholders' equity of $107.5 billion as of June 27, 2026, up from $73.7 billion at fiscal year-end 2025.
qualitative.filing_summary_8k: This 8-K, dated July 30, 2026, discloses under Item 2.02 that Apple issued a press release announcing its financial results for the third fiscal quarter ended June 27, 2026, attached as an exhibit; the 8-K itself does not include the detailed financial figures beyond referencing the attached press release.
qualitative.moat_explanation: The 10-K describes Apple's integrated ecosystem (proprietary hardware, operating systems, software, and services), a large portfolio of patents, trademarks, and copyrights, and a strong brand/third-party ecosystem as principal competitive factors. However, the filing itself acknowledges the Company holds only a 'minority market share' in smartphones, PCs, tablets, and wearables, and faces intense price-based competition, tempering the strength of this moat.
red_flags: Company explicitly states it has a minority market share in global smartphone, PC, tablet, and wearables markets and faces aggressive price competition
Reliance on single or limited-source suppliers and custom components creates supply concentration risk
Majority of manufacturing performed by outsourcing partners concentrated in China mainland, India, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, and Vietnam, exposing the Company to geopolitical and trade risk
New U.S. tariffs beginning fiscal Q2 2025 (including on China, India, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Vietnam, EU) already impacting costs and gross margin, with uncertain further impact
Section 232 investigation into semiconductor and related imports adds regulatory uncertainty
Company states gross margins will be subject to volatility and downward pressure going forward
